A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FOCUS dataset and REFLECT benchmark. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial additions and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original VLM evaluations on three tasks, dataset quality checks, and salary significance tests in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original evaluations and adds empirical robustness checks, audits, uncertainty analyses, and exploratory coverage extensions.

M1.justification: The core face-editing pipeline, FOCUS construction method, and three-task REFLECT framework remain unchanged. Alternative editors, prompts, and presentation conditions are evaluated as auxiliary experimental variations.

E1.justification: Appendices C.7–C.8 add MCQ evaluations for software developer and construction laborer, plus an exploratory androgynous-presentation condition. Mirroring and cropping also extend tested image conditions. These are targeted extensions; the original six-occupation, 480-image benchmark remains intact.

E2.justification: The five-model evaluation panel and VisBias comparison are retained. Appendix C.2 newly compares the original gemini-3-pro-image-preview editor against gpt-5-image through matched MCQ evaluations using GPT, Gemini, and Qwen.

E3.justification: V2 adds protocols for spatial transformations, editor substitution, explanation-augmented answers, template removal, and stochastic decoding at temperature 0.7, plus polarization metrics. Figure 8 revises the 2AFC description from the same person in two versions to different people edited from one photograph. This documents a prompt revision without establishing that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: V1 mainly provides face-localization and demographic-label checks. V2 adds extensive tests of face–body mismatch, expression drift, mirroring/cropping, biography quality, prompt framing, filtering, position bias, editor dependence, template sensitivity, explanations, and decoding randomness in Appendices B–C.

E5.justification: V1 already reports cluster-robust salary significance tests, retained as v2 Table 13. V2 additionally reports template-cluster bootstrap and Wilson confidence intervals and explicitly adds stochastic repeated sampling: five runs per MCQ query and three for Income 2AFC.

E6.justification: The original MCQ JSD tables and salary p-values are retained as v2 Tables 2, 3, and 13. Substantial new results include polarization, cross-model correlations, filtering diagnostics, robustness outcomes, and coverage extensions. Examples include 12.1% expression drift and 0.940 correlation after expression filtering; these are newly reported analyses.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 introduces formal definitions of the polarization index and extreme-cell rate over pairwise win rates. Existing win-rate, mean-gap, and JSD definitions remain substantively unchanged; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: controlled real-photo counterfactuals, FOCUS, REFLECT's three tasks, and persistent demographic disparities that vary across tasks and models. Condensing four contribution bullets to three does not remove the empirical contribution, which remains stated elsewhere.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations concerning residual editing artifacts, scenario-dependent refusals, template stability, and decoding sensitivity. It distinguishes robust distributional disparities from weaker mean effects, limits cross-editor conclusions to the tested MCQ subset, and explicitly distinguishes visual gender presentation from gender identity.

D1.justification: The abstract newly supplies a code repository link. Appendices add editor and evaluator identifiers, crop-construction details, biography-audit criteria, subset construction, and sampling settings. Existing main-task prompt templates and implementation descriptions are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of VIGNETTE, hiring halo effects, multimodal debiasing, modality bias/conflict, and face-perception research, alongside additional model citations. These broaden supporting context while retaining the original positioning around realism and control in counterfactual bias evaluation.

P1.justification: V2 condenses and edits the introduction and findings, updates affiliations and corresponding-author information, and adds acknowledgments. Appendix subsections expand to organize the new analyses, while the main narrative structure remains substantially the same.

P2.justification: V2 adds ten analytical tables and redraws the main and appendix result charts with revised legends, axes, annotations, and panel arrangements. Figure 5 becomes full-width, and existing figures and tables are redistributed through the expanded appendices.

improvement.justification: V1's attribution argument relied mainly on face-localization and label checks. V2 directly tests several residual confounds and quantifies template and decoding uncertainty, substantially strengthening empirical credibility. Table 9 also reveals weaker mean effects alongside robust distributional disparities. Signed gaps remain sensitive to editor choice in Table 8, limiting claims of complete robustness, but the added validation addresses important weaknesses in v1.
